*** TIMESTAMPS DIFFER BY MORE THAN A DAY. Published pre-window (03:12 BST Sunday); UPDATED 06:36 BST this morning. Treat the global-reaction roundup as live, the core attack facts as carried-forward. ***
"World condemns deadly Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia's Riyadh airport"
Standfirst: "Trump denounces 'terrible' attack and says the US is evaluating whether to join Saudi Arabia's offensive against the Houthis."

*** THIS SETTLES THE RIYADH ORDINAL ***
"Saudi Arabia has accused Yemen's Houthis of killing at least 12 people and wounding 300 others in a THIRD ATTACK ON THE RIYADH INTERNATIONAL AIRPORT THIS WEEK."
=> SATURDAY 10 OCT was the THIRD strike on Riyadh airport. SUNDAY 11 OCT was therefore the FOURTH - which reconciles Al Jazeera's "struck four times in the past five days".
=> The coordinator's "third strike" label belongs to SATURDAY's attack, not Sunday's. The BBC's "second in two days" counts only Sat+Sun.
"It was the deadliest attack on the kingdom in more than a decade."
Victims of Saturday's attack per the General Authority of Civil Aviation: four Saudis, two Bangladeshis and one person each from the United States, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt.
Context: Saudi Arabia is waging an air campaign against the Houthis to support the ground war by Yemeni government forces.

*** TRUMP ON JOINING THE WAR - EXACT WORDS ***
Trump described the attack as "terrible" and said he "will be speaking" with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman (MBS) soon. He said he was evaluating whether the US should join the war against the Houthis:
"We may. We're gonna look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We'll move very quickly."
(Guardian's version of the same remarks, on whether to join the Saudi campaign: "We're going to look into it." BBC's: the US would "make a decision" and "move very quickly".)
CONTEXT FOR WEIGHING THIS: per the Guardian, about 200 US military advisers are already in Saudi Arabia and the US is assisting with intelligence cooperation and targeting, but "the US has not directly taken part in fighting against the Houthis."

*** WHO ELSE CONDEMNED IT ***
- US Secretary of State MARCO RUBIO: said the attack killed an American and called for an end to "these reprehensible attacks". On X: "We stand with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and its people and extend our condolences to the victims and their families."
- UN Secretary-General ANTONIO GUTERRES, on X: "deeply shocked", strongly condemns "Saturday's lethal attack by the Houthis"; said attacks on civilians and civilian infrastructure violated international law and "must cease immediately".
- HANS GRUNDBERG, UN special envoy for Yemen: the deadly strikes on civilian airports represent "a grave escalation". "Such actions pose a serious threat to regional security, perpetuate cycles of violence and complicate even more peace efforts for Yemen."
- EGYPT's Ministry of Foreign Affairs: "strong condemnation", denouncing the Houthis' "flagrant violation" of international law and "disregard" for the safety of citizens.
- QATAR (Doha): condemned the attack as a "serious violation of Saudi sovereignty and a direct threat to the security of the region, the safety of civilians, civil facilities and air navigation"; expressed full solidarity and supported "all legitimate measures" the kingdom "takes to preserve its sovereignty, security and safety of its territories".
- PAKISTAN PM SHEHBAZ SHARIF: condemned the "heinous attack". On X: "Attacks targeting civilians and vital infrastructure are utterly unacceptable and pose a serious threat to regional peace and stability." Reaffirmed Pakistan's "steadfast commitment to Saudi Arabia's sovereignty, territorial integrity". (Note: the person killed in SUNDAY's strike was a Pakistani resident.)
- Jordan also listed (text truncated at fetch).
